title: Marguerite and the Inheritance
premise: Retired detective Jonah Galloway, now barely keeping the doors of a failing bookshop open, receives a confession letter for a thirty-year-old drowning—postmarked the day after Marguerite Ashcombe's funeral. The letter claims Marguerite's death was murder and that the writer will confess publicly in seven days unless Jonah proves otherwise first. As Jonah reopens alibis from 1994, they discover the letter writer is someone whose life Marguerite quietly saved—and that Jonah's own name appears in her will, a bequest they never knew existed. In the end, Jonah exposes the killer: Marguerite's devoted caretaker, who poisoned her slowly to protect a secret she'd unearthed about the town's founding families, and Jonah must choose between closing the case cleanly or revealing that their own late mother helped bury the original crime.
about_author: Casper Brightwater is the pen name of a former small-town newspaper reporter who spent a decade covering obituaries and court dockets before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who thought their pasts had safely expired.

chapters.title: Postmarked Yesterday
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Three days after Marguerite Ashcombe's funeral, an unsigned confession letter arrives at the bookshop claiming her drowning thirty years ago was murder, with a seven-day deadline. Jonah, who owes Marguerite a debt from their last case, reluctantly begins digging through old case files. Emotional beat: reluctant awakening—the pull of unfinished business over quiet retreat.

chapters.title: The Alibi Season
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, intercut with Marguerite's 1994 diary entries. Jonah interviews the four witnesses whose alibis have held for three decades, finding each account polished like a stone—too perfect. The diary reveals Marguerite knew she was being watched in her final weeks. Emotional beat: mounting unease as certainty curdles into suspicion of everyone, including old friends.

chapters.title: What the Will Buried
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The reading of the will reveals a bequest to Jonah—a locked box containing evidence Marguerite gathered about the 1994 drowning and the town founders' fraud it exposed. The caretaker, Edmund Voss, grows desperate as Jonah closes in, sabotaging the shop and threatening the deadline witness. Emotional beat: betrayal and resolve—Jonah realizes staying invisible made them complicit.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Tide
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. At the tide flats where Marguerite drowned, Jonah stages a public reckoning on the seventh day, forcing Voss to confess to her slow poisoning and confronting the town—and their own mother's role—in the original cover-up. The bookshop gains unexpected visitors drawn by the truth. Emotional beat: bittersweet belonging; Jonah finally accepts that some inheritances can't be refused.
